headline_marked: [[Childhood dreams of sci-fi robots]] drive Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, and Masayoshi Son in the Physical AI race
headline: Childhood dreams of sci-fi robots drive Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, and Masayoshi Son in the Physical AI race
summary: Tech leaders like Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, and Masayoshi Son are pushing the Physical AI frontier, openly citing iconic fictional robots like C-3PO, R2-D2, and Astro Boy as their inspiration.
details: The frontier of artificial intelligence is rapidly expanding beyond digital displays into our physical reality, a shift known as Physical AI or Embodied AI. This involves intelligence that understands physical laws and operates within our world.

Behind the relentless pursuit of Physical AI by engineers and executives lies a profound motivation: the desire to build the robots they fell in love with in childhood stories. From Doraemon to Star Wars, fictional AI serves as a direct engineering compass.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk envisions Optimus as a personal C-3PO and R2-D2, capable of domestic chores and caregiving. He projects mass-production costs to drop below $20,000–$30,000, aiming for an "Age of Abundance."

NVIDIA's Jensen Huang declared Physical AI as the "next wave," showcasing miniature bipedal droids at GTC. These robots, modeled after Star Wars BD-units, learned balance and emotional mannerisms via reinforcement learning in Isaac Sim.

Mark Zuckerberg's 2016 personal challenge was to build a J.A.R.V.I.S.-like AI for his home. His experience highlighted the difficulty of connecting fragmented physical devices, influencing Meta's long-term research into Embodied AI and ambient wearables.

In Japan, humanoid robotics was directly inspired by post-war manga and anime, with Honda's ASIMO project sparked by a mandate to "Build Astro Boy." SoftBank's Masayoshi Son also cited Astro Boy and Doraemon as inspirations for emotional robots like Pepper.

The development of Physical AI combines powerful "Brains" like LLMs and VLMs for multimodal reasoning with advanced "Bodies" featuring actuators, bipedal balance, and tactile sensors. This integration aims to create humanoids with sophisticated cognitive and physical capabilities.

headline_marked: [[polylinedb launches as a task and memory store]] for cloud agents on Cloudflare
headline: polylinedb launches as a task and memory store for cloud agents on Cloudflare
summary: polylinedb, a new open-source tool, provides a shared task and memory store for local and cloud agents. It leverages Cloudflare Workers and D1, enabling seamless knowledge sharing and task management across environments.
details: polylinedb, a new task and memory store, is now available on npm (version 0.1.0). It allows local tools and cloud agents to share tasks and project knowledge, running within a user's own Cloudflare account.

The tool addresses the challenge of maintaining consistent records across different agent environments. It solves the problem of local records not being accessible to cloud agents, eliminating the need for manual syncing or separate copies.

For example, a local agent can record a bug finding as an issue, which a cloud agent can then read before working on a fix. Users can inspect the same record from their laptop, ensuring continuity across development stages.
The architecture uses a Cloudflare Worker to accept HTTP requests from a local CLI and remote MCP calls from cloud hosts. Cloudflare's serverless SQLite service, D1, is used to store all records.

Agents can create issues, search earlier findings, append comments, or update progress through either the CLI or cloud interfaces. The cloud-first design ensures records remain accessible regardless of the host or session.

Tasks are used to record work that needs to be done, while memory retains findings and constraints for future work. This allows critical project knowledge, like migration requirements, to persist beyond individual tasks.

Authentication is handled by Cloudflare Access using OAuth, with polylinedb checking the authenticated identity against an allowlist. The system avoids placing client secrets in prompts, using browser login and local credential storage for the CLI.

polylinedb also features concurrency handling, rejecting stale updates to prevent overwrites and recognizing retries to avoid duplicate tasks. This design accounts for agents working concurrently over a network, though multi-person operation has not been extensively tested.
An independent local SQLite mode is also available, providing an explicit migration path to the cloud. For shared records, the cloud connection is preferred over synchronized local copies.
The developer successfully used polylinedb with various AI models, including Cursor Cloud, Codex Cloud, and Claude, for creating issues, reading them, and adding comments via MCP.
